correctness.rationale: The incidence lower bound uses at most five points on two Fano lines. The complete 32767-form binary-quartic census produces 448 exactly-three-point rationally smooth tangent coverings. All 168 invertible coordinate matrices produce five disjoint orbits of sizes 84,84,84,28,168. In each of the three affine charts, characteristic-two reduced Groebner bases give the unit ideal for four representatives; the fifth has a singularity over F_4. Thus exactly 364 curves in four orbits are geometrically smooth. The delivered standalone verifier was executed successfully and directly checks derivative evaluations, group orbits, and rational incidence; the claim is finite, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: Asgarli--Ghioca 2023 introduces tangent filling but does not classify this binary genus-three extremum. Nart--Ritzenthaler 2003 classifies all smooth binary plane quartics up to isomorphism but does not state rational tangent-line covering conditions or the four-orbit equality census. This exact incidence invariant is not listed in their tables, and its calculation requires additional rational Gauss-map checks. Homma--Kim gives minimal-degree plane-filling curves, which have seven rational points in this case. Extensive targeted searches identified no explicit or stronger covering result. Remaining risk: another indexed or unindexed tabulation may have performed the same tangent refinement.
residual_risks: Existing complete genus-three quartic normal forms may permit a short derivation of the refined tangent classification; no precomputed claim/table was found, but implicit coverage cannot be absolutely excluded.
Unindexed finite-geometric enumerations of rational tangent pencils for quartics over F_2 may exist.

value.rationale: The motivating question asks how few rational points can nevertheless supply tangent lines covering an entire finite projective plane. The incidence bound of three is sharp already for smooth genus-three canonical curves, and the equality cases admit a complete projective classification with four symmetry types. The new incidence invariant separates center-on-curve (252 equations) and center-off-curve (112 equations), contrasting sharply with plane-filling quartics requiring all seven rational points. The result is a natural exact extremal classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or generic smoothness example.
